【分支1 · P01】请阅读下面这首诗,然后回答随后三题(1-7打分)。
[Branch 1 · P01] Read the sonnet, then rate the next three items.
The year turns down its page, a fading gold,
And swallows chart their long and silent way;
The fields, once warm, are now a story told
In stubble gray beneath a lingering day.
The garden’s last, late rose surrenders breath
To winds that carry rumors of the frost;
Each bough lets go its hold, and what was health
Becomes a memory, lovely and soon lost.
Yet I, who watch the quiet world unbind,
Find no despair in what must fall and flee;
The heart, like earth, must leave its bloom behind
To learn the patience of the coming tree.
So let this parting be a gentle art—
I keep the warmth, and let the season start.

【分支1 · P02】请阅读下面这首诗,然后回答随后三题(1-7打分)。
[Branch 1 · P02] Read the sonnet, then rate the next three items.
The orchard’s last, bruised apple drops its hold,
And creaking branches bare their knuckled bone;
The wind, a keeper now grown gray and cold,
Unlocks the gate where summer’s warm light shone.
I watch the amber leaves, a scattered fleet,
Set sail upon the gutter’s shallow tide,
And mourn the crisp, bright mornings we would meet
When dew hung heavy on the hillside’s pride.
But in this falling, find a quieter grace—
The slow, deliberate closing of a door,
The settling of dust in a sunlit space,
The harvest’s weight laid down upon the floor.
So let the season’s rigor have its way;
I’ll keep the ember’s glow for darker day.

【分支2 · P03】请阅读下面这首诗,然后回答随后三题(1-7打分)。
[Branch 2 · P03] Read the sonnet, then rate the next three items.
The wind strips gold from branches, one by one,
And bears the tattered leaves on hurried wings;
The amber light of afternoon is done,
And silence settles where the robin sings.
The garden paths are strewn with faded blooms,
The scented air grows thin and sharp with frost;
A lonely swallow traces through the glooms,
And all the summer’s promises are lost.
But O, this parting is not final grief—
It is the earth’s slow breathing, deep and still,
A turning inward, root and sleeping leaf,
A quiet trust that answers winter’s will.
So let the cold wind take what it must take—
The seed remembers what the season makes.

【分支2 · P04】请阅读下面这首诗,然后回答随后三题(1-7打分)。
[Branch 2 · P04] Read the sonnet, then rate the next three items.
The maple sheds its coins upon the walk,
A copper flood that clatters at my heel;
The branches twist in skeletal, slow talk,
And strip the final gold they used to feel.
The wind, a workman with a greedy blade,
Shears off the clinging vestiges of grace,
And every tumbling leaf becomes a shade
That cannot find its summer resting place.
But look! The orchard, stripped of all pretense,
Reveals the iron lattice of its boughs,
A stark and sudden architecture, dense
With promise that the frozen earth allows.
So let the season’s ruin be complete;
What falls to ground must rise on stronger feet.

【分支3 · P05】请阅读下面这首诗,然后回答随后三题(1-7打分)。
[Branch 3 · P05] Read the sonnet, then rate the next three items.
The streetlight hums a pale and constant note,
The asphalt gleams with rain that fell at noon.
A single window, high above, afloat,
Holds back the dark with one unsteady moon.
The traffic’s distant pulse, a muted drum,
Beats time for no one walking here but me.
The empty benches wait for hours to come,
And storefront glass repeats what I can’t see.
This solitude is not a thing to fear,
But like a room where echoes learn their name;
The city breathes, and I am merely here,
A leaf that drifted from a hidden flame.
So let the night unspool its silent thread—
I’ll walk until the stars have gone to bed.
【分支3 · P05】张力 Tension 评分 (1-7)
【分支3 · P05】象征/意象 Symbol(Imagery) 评分 (1-7)

【分支3 · P06】请阅读下面这首诗,然后回答随后三题(1-7打分)。
[Branch 3 · P06] Read the sonnet, then rate the next three items.
The streetlamp hums its thin and jaundiced song,
A weary chorus to the sleeping stone.
The city's breath is shallow, held too long,
And I am utterly, and quite alone.
My footsteps make a lonely, ticking sound
That bounces off the glass and fades to null,
As if the dark were swallowing the ground
On which I walk, a pathway rendered null.
A single window glows a sulfur square,
A distant ship upon a sea of black.
I do not know the soul who kindles there,
Nor does he know the ghost that wanders back.
So I will keep this vigil, cold and deep,
And hold my solitude till morning's keep.

【分支4 · P07】请阅读下面这首诗,然后回答随后三题(1-7打分)。
[Branch 4 · P07] Read the sonnet, then rate the next three items.
The city sheds its clamor, stone by stone,
And streets grow deep with silence, cool and vast,
Where every window holds a lamp alone,
A ghost of daylight that has overpast.
The traffic’s roar has dwindled to a sigh,
A distant siren’s thin, forgotten thread;
The neon signs blink out against the sky,
And all the hurried multitudes are dead.
But I—I am the pulse that will not sleep,
The sharpened breath that cuts the hollow air;
I am the vigil that the shadows keep,
The one who names the darkness, and the dare.
So let the sleepers dream their borrowed peace—
I’ll walk this night until the morning’s lease.

【分支4 · P08】请阅读下面这首诗,然后回答随后三题(1-7打分)。
[Branch 4 · P08] Read the sonnet, then rate the next three items.
The streetlamp hums a thin electric psalm
To empty sidewalks glossed with recent rain.
My footsteps mark the pavement, cold and calm,
A lonely meter tapped in minor strain.
The windows overhead are shutters drawn,
Each yellow square a story locked inside,
While I, a transient in the neon dawn,
Trace cables where the sleeping city’s tied.
But then the wind, a sudden, hungry gust,
Tears at the awning’s seam with ragged nails,
And from the gutter’s dark, a scatter-rust
Whirls up to mock the peace that daylight veils.
So let the fragile glass of quiet break—
I’ll walk this shard-strewn night for my own sake.

【分支5 · P09】请阅读下面这首诗,然后回答随后三题(1-7打分)。
[Branch 5 · P09] Read the sonnet, then rate the next three items.
The well of years is deep, and I descend
By crumbling steps where moss and silence meet,
To find the waters that my youth would spend,
A quiet current, cold against the feet.
Each ripple is a face I used to know,
A voice that bends the light of what has been,
And in the glass, the shadows come and go—
The rain that fell, the river's unseen skin.
I cup my hands to hold what will not stay,
The liquid moment slipping through my grip,
And what I drink is only yesterday,
A taste of salt upon the waiting lip.
So let the stream go on, and let it be—
The memory of water stays in me.

【分支5 · P10】请阅读下面这首诗,然后回答随后三题(1-7打分)。
[Branch 5 · P10] Read the sonnet, then rate the next three items.
The river keeps what daylight cannot hold,
A sunken bell of hours, a coin of years,
And in its murk, a story half-told,
That drifts on currents, deaf to falling tears.
I wade where the shallows ripple, and sift
The silt for a face that the flood erased,
My fingers net a glint, a patient gift—
A shard of mirror where a smile was placed.
But the water tightens, a cold, closing fist,
And the glass slips back to the breathing mud,
Where the shape that I chased no longer exists,
Only the ache of a remembered flood.
So I walk the bank, and the current goes,
While the river keeps what my heart bestows.

【分支5 · P10】象征/意象 Symbol(Imagery) 评分 (1-7)

【分支6 · P11】请阅读下面这首诗,然后回答随后三题(1-7打分)。
[Branch 6 · P11] Read the sonnet, then rate the next three items.
The mind is not a ledger, but a sea
That keeps its ledgers in a liquid sleep,
And every wave a thrice-remembered plea
From coasts the sunken years have ceased to keep.
I cast a stone of thought—and watch it fall
Through fathoms where the drowned days turn and gleam,
Their faces blurred against a coral wall,
The wreck of every unaccomplished dream.
But now the tide turns hard, and salt-stung air
Unravels what the patient deep has spun—
The bright particular grief I used to bear
Comes surfacing, a ghost beneath the sun,
And I must drink that brine, must taste the whole
Cold archive of the water in my soul.
【分支6 · P11】张力 Tension 评分 (1-7)
【分支6 · P11】象征/意象 Symbol(Imagery) 评分 (1-7)
【分支6 · P11】节奏/韵律 Rhythm 评分 (1-7)

【分支6 · P12】请阅读下面这首诗,然后回答随后三题(1-7打分)。
[Branch 6 · P12] Read the sonnet, then rate the next three items.
The current, braided bright, unspools the glass
Where every sunken face I knew is kept;
I drag the river’s hem, the silted mass
Of hours that the living currents swept.
A stone I touched when autumn fouled the weir
Still hums against my palm its cold refrain—
The pressure of a thumbprint, sharp and clear,
That fades if I should lift my hand again.
Then sudden stormlight cracks the surface wide:
The wreck of that old bridge, its stanchions torn,
Breaks upward through the flood, and I must ride
The spume that keeps a name I had forsworn.
So let the deep forget what I have held—
One gasp of air, and all the waves are quelled.
